label: Barakat Gallery X.0552
summary: Jewish Babylonian Aramaic incantation bowl for Hurmizdad son of Mamy and his family, offered by Barakat Gallery.

source.title: Terracotta Incantation Bowl with Aramaic Inscription, 500 CE–800 CE
source.citation: Barakat Gallery, ‘Terracotta Incantation Bowl with Aramaic Inscription,’ stock X.0552, online record 54886, accessed 4 September 2026.
source.notes: The 2019 listing and its unsigned translation are discussed by Nils H. Korsvoll in Journal of Art Crime 23 (2020).

claims.value_text: Hurmizdad son of Mamy, his wife, sons, and daughters
Protection from dreams of the night and day
No pre-2019 ownership history stated in the current listing

texts.content: Sealed and countersealed in the house and dwelling of Hurmizdad son of Mamy, his wife, sons and daughters, from dreams of night and day; the spell invokes seven seals and quotes Zechariah 3:2 and Deuteronomy 6:4.

events.details: Documented as offered online during Korsvoll's June 2019 market survey; current page remains enquiry-only.

label: Cincinnati Skirball Museum A/1331
summary: Mandaic bowl protecting Mihdanahik daughter of Liula and Mshirtsai son of Mhudanduk against curses.

source.title: Mandaic Bowl
source.citation: Cincinnati Skirball Museum, ‘Mandaic Bowl,’ A/1331, object feature published 17 July 2021.

claims.value_text: Mihdanahik daughter of Liula; Mshirtsai son of Mhudanduk
Repulsion and binding of curses and incantations in the four corners of the house

texts.content: The spell overturns, binds, and repulses curses directed at Mihdanahik daughter of Liula, invokes the angel Tabaq for Mshirtsai son of Mhudanduk, and commands that hostile incantations remain distant.

events.details: Museum purchase with funds provided by Dr. Helen Iglauer Glueck.
